title: A tighter bound for four seven-cycles
oneLine: An exact finite exclusion narrows the independence-number interval to 108–112; the precise answer remains open.
abstract: This computer-assisted candidate excludes every 113-word independent set in the fourth strong power of the seven-cycle. A complete cubic catalogue, exhaustive band-allocation checks and integer completion certificates give 108 ≤ α(C₇^⊠4) ≤ 112, improving the historical upper endpoint 115 recorded in 2019. Auxiliary results classify maximum-square boundary traces, exclude the zero-saturation-excess balanced 112 case, determine the square-factor gadget maximum 106 and certify feasibility of a specified two-block moment relaxation at 109–112. These scoped results do not determine the exact independence number or Shannon capacity.
statusDetail: Unrefereed computer-assisted mathematical candidate. Producer-side exact replay and internal semantic checks are distinct from unaffiliated reproduction, formal verification and external peer review.
evidence: Complete cubic census; exhaustive adjacent and nonadjacent band allocations; additions-only RUP checks and exact integer completion inequalities. Acceptance receipts identify the complete replay scope.
narration:
Imagine sending a four-symbol message, where each symbol has seven possible values arranged around a circle. Neighbouring values can be confused. Two messages are safely distinguishable if at least one position separates them by more than one step around that circle.

How many messages can we choose so that every pair is distinguishable? A construction with one hundred and eight messages has been known since two thousand and two. The historical upper bound was one hundred and fifteen.

This candidate lowers that upper bound to one hundred and twelve. The exact answer remains unknown: it could still be any integer from one hundred and eight to one hundred and twelve.

The proof starts by supposing that one hundred and thirteen messages exist. Split them into seven layers according to one symbol. Each pair of neighbouring layers can contain at most thirty-three messages. Counting these overlapping pairs forces at least two to reach that maximum.

There are two possibilities: the maximum pairs share a layer, or they do not. The evidence package checks both cases exhaustively, using a complete catalogue of smaller codes. Every surviving partial arrangement is ruled out by an inequality evaluated with exact integers.

The package also records useful limits on future approaches. One particular construction using two-dimensional ingredients can reach at most one hundred and six messages. A specified moment relaxation is too weak to settle the remaining gap. Neither statement rules out a better construction by other means.

Readers can inspect the mathematical reductions, source code, certificates and full replay instructions. This is an unrefereed computer-assisted candidate, not a determination of Shannon capacity or an independently formalised proof.

This is Evidence Press, A tighter bound for four seven-cycles, dated the fifth of October twenty twenty-six. The paper and evidence are linked on the release page. This synthetic AI voice is an explanation, not additional scientific evidence.
